steps.en: Report headings: Use the same headings every time so readers find facts fast.
Numbers to quote: Quote ejection fraction as a number with its method: Simpson biplane or visual estimate.
Quote left atrial volume index with 34 ml per sq m as the upper normal limit.
Quote tricuspid peak velocity with 2.8 m per s as the upper normal limit.

Pitfalls: Adjectives without numbers cannot be checked, so never say moderate dysfunction without the ejection fraction. Name the method behind every number, since a visual estimate and a Simpson value carry different weight.

analogy.en: Report headings: Indication, rhythm, heart rate, blood pressure and quality.

spot.en: Report headings: Indication, rhythm, heart rate, blood pressure and quality.
Left ventricle: size, thickness, regional motion and ejection fraction.
Left atrium and right heart with pulmonary pressure estimate.
Valves: morphology plus grade with supporting numbers.
Pericardium, aorta and conclusion with follow up plan.

todo.en: Presentation order: State the indication, the rhythm, the heart rate and the study quality with any limits.
Give left heart size and function: diameters, wall thickness, volumes and ejection fraction with method.
Give right heart size and function with the estimated pulmonary pressure and its basis.
Describe each valve in order with the grade and the two numbers behind it.
Report the pericardium, aorta and any mass, thrombus or shunt.
Close with one conclusion that answers the referral question.

remember.en: Close with a conclusion that answers the referral question.

why.en: Context and quality frame every number that follows.
The reader asked a question, so answer it last and plainly.

q.en: Ejection fraction is 45 percent by visual estimate. How do you quote it?

why.en: Number plus method beats any adjective.
